task_message:
Case N19: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 221x221x187 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
The segmentation is complete and saved.

**Summary:** The peripheral nerve sheath tumor in this T2-weighted (fat-suppressed) study is a well-circumscribed, markedly hyperintense oval mass in the anterior subcutaneous tissue of the limb, showing a central darker "target-like" core. I started the mask with a point prompt on a mark inside the mass, which the model propagated into a 3D segmentation matching the lesion. I then:

- Verified the extent slice-by-slice in all three planes (upper/lower poles at axial slices 35–78, plus coronal and sagittal ends).
- Removed a small stray component (0.1 mL) corresponding to the bright skin marker lying outside the body anterior to the mass.
- Confirmed that the separate bright structures (skin markers, vessels along the fascial planes) were excluded.
- Checked automatic candidate proposals (none found) and the final five-panel-per-plane review, where the outline tracked the bright tumor boundary and the past-the-mask slices showed no residual lesion.

**Final mask:** 18.6 mL, a single connected component, with a confidence of **high**.
